cues.en: I applied to the city in early 2014 to turn my coin-operated laundry into housing. We sit at ground zero of anti-gentrification in San Francisco. Getting this property approved has so far taken longer than it took the United States to win World War II. I've spent 1.2 million.
cues.zh: 我在2014年初向市里申请，把自助洗衣店改建成住房。我们正处在旧金山反绅士化运动的风口浪尖。这个房产的审批耗时已经超过美国打赢二战的时间。我已经花了120万美元。

cues.en: The Board of Supervisors denied the project because it cast a partial shadow on an adjacent schoolyard. If you're wondering why housing in San Francisco is expensive, they make it expensive here. It is intentional.
cues.zh: 监事会否决了这个项目，因为它给邻近的校园投下了部分阴影。如果你想知道旧金山的住房为什么这么贵，是这里的人让它变贵的。这是故意的。

cues.en: Sky high rents in San Francisco. They pay $7,000 a month. 54% rent increase. It's just been such a steady climb. Dramatically in the last five to ten years. It's astounding. The sky high new record. Once working class neighborhoods transformed. San Francisco has become the most expensive city to live in in the nation. As its population has boomed over the past few decades, developers have found it almost impossible to build new housing.
cues.zh: 旧金山房租高得离谱。他们每月付7000美元。租金涨了54%。就是一路稳步攀升。过去五到十年涨得特别猛。令人震惊。新高纪录。曾经的工薪阶层社区被改造。旧金山已成为全美居住成本最高的城市。随着过去几十年人口激增，开发商发现几乎不可能建新住房。

cues.en: The story of one small developer in particular shines a light on what's gone wrong in the Golden Gate City. San Francisco is the worst place in the country to try to do development, and the mission is the worst place in San Francisco. Bob Tillman has owned a coin-operated laundromat here in the Mission District for 20 years. In 2013, he decided to tear it down and build an eight-story, 75-unit apartment building. Since nobody lives above the laundry, the project wouldn't displace any residents.
cues.zh: 尤其是一位小开发商的故事，照出了这座金门城市哪里出了问题。旧金山是全美最难搞开发的地方，而Mission区又是旧金山最难的地方。Bob Tillman在Mission区拥有一家自助洗衣店已经20年了。2013年，他决定拆掉它，建一栋八层、75个单元的公寓楼。由于洗衣店上方没有人居住，这个项目不会迫使任何居民搬迁。

cues.en: It would also be in a popular area near multiple public transit stops, which qualified it for a streamlined approval process under state law. And the site had another major advantage for avoiding red tape. It was already zoned for housing. If you can't build here, then you can't build anywhere. But San Francisco developers are required to get explicit permission from city officials for any new construction. So in early 2014, Tillman began submitting paperwork to the planning department.
cues.zh: 它还会位于一个热门区域，靠近多个公共交通站点，这使它有资格根据州法律获得简化审批流程。而且这块地还有个更大的优势，可以避开繁琐手续。它已经被划为住宅用地。如果这里都建不了，那哪里都建不了。但旧金山的开发商必须获得市官员的明确许可才能进行任何新建设。所以在2014年初，蒂尔曼开始向规划部门提交文书。

cues.en: I went through an environmental review, application for conditional use permit, a planning commission hearing, which turned into a second planning commission hearing. The commission ordered a detailed historical review based on a claim that various community groups had offices on the property in the 1970s and 80s. The resulting 137-page study concluded that the laundry did not merit historic landmark status. That study cost me $23,000 and delayed me another four months.
cues.zh: 我经历了环境审查、有条件使用许可申请、规划委员会听证会，后来又变成了第二次规划委员会听证会。委员会下令进行详细的历史审查，理由是有各种社区团体在20世纪70年代和80年代曾在这块地上办公。结果那份137页的研究得出结论，这家洗衣店不值得获得历史地标地位。那份研究花了我23000美元，还又拖了我四个月。

cues.en: In late 2017, the Planning Commission was finally ready to vote on Tillman's project, three and a half years after he first applied to build. But that's when the real fight started. The mission is the place where you have the biggest and most vocal anti-jectification groups. City law says that any individual or group, no matter where they live, can pay a $617 fee to appeal a decision by the Planning Commission. In this case, the challenge came from an organization called Calle Benti Quatro. Welcome to Calle Benti Quatro Latino Cultural District.
cues.zh: 2017年底，规划委员会终于准备对蒂尔曼的项目投票，此时距他首次申请建设已经过去了三年半。但真正的战斗才刚刚开始。米慎区是反绅士化团体最大、声音最响的地方。城市法律规定，任何个人或团体，无论住在哪里，都可以支付617美元的费用来对规划委员会的决定提出上诉。在这个案例中，挑战来自一个叫Calle Benti Quatro的组织。欢迎来到Calle Benti Quatro拉丁文化区。

cues.en: Calvitiguato has been actively involved with development in the LCD and greater mission to make sure development is equitable and that it truly benefits and meets the needs of the community. The mission is an historically working class district where less than two decades ago residents were mostly Hispanic. But the Latino population has been shrinking as wealthier white residents move in and housing prices here are rising even faster than in the rest of San Francisco.
cues.zh: Calvitiguato 一直积极参与 LCD 及更大 Mission 区的发展，确保发展公平，真正造福并满足社区需求。Mission 历来是工人阶级社区，不到二十年前居民还以西班牙裔为主。但随着更富裕的白人居民迁入，拉丁裔人口不断减少，这里房价上涨甚至比旧金山其他地区还快。

cues.en: Calle Bentiquattro, which declined Reason's interview request, is one of several neighborhood organizations dedicated to stopping gentrification in the mission.
cues.zh: Calle Bentiquattro 拒绝了 Reason 的采访请求；它是致力于阻止 Mission 区绅士化的几个社区组织之一。

cues.en: What they say is they are defending poor people. That actually building more housing results in more displacement. This has especially been exasperated by the increase in high paying jobs that have come to the city and has resulted in a construction explosion and displacement by exclusion. There is displacement going on in the mission. Latinos are moving out of the mission. I don't think anyone's arguing about that.
cues.zh: 他们说自己在保护穷人，说实际建造更多住房会导致更多居民被迫迁离。城市里高薪岗位增加尤其加剧了这一点，带来了建设热潮和排斥性置换。Mission 区确实在发生置换，拉丁裔正在搬离 Mission。我不认为有人会否认这一点。

cues.en: Todd David is the executive director of the San Francisco Housing Action Coalition. It is much better for the residents who live there now to provide housing for people who want to live in that neighborhood. The reason that the displacement is taking place in the mission is because we haven't built any housing there in 15 years. People are going to want to live in the mission, whether we build housing there or not. When you have people with resources competing with people with fewer resources for a limited commodity.
cues.zh: Todd David 是 San Francisco Housing Action Coalition 的执行主任。对现在住在那里的居民来说，为想住进该社区的人提供住房要好得多。Mission 区发生置换，是因为我们 15 年没在那里建任何住房。不管我们建不建住房，人们都会想住进 Mission。当有资源的人与资源较少的人争夺有限的商品时。

cues.en: Who's going to end up with that commodity? In the mission, rent control has allowed some long-term tenants to stay put amid rising market prices. But rent control discourages new housing construction and merely delays the displacement of residents. As soon as a tenant dies or moves out, landlords can raise the rent as much as they like. This project provides only a minimum number of affordable units in a sense of neighborhood. That is not inclusive towards our Latino community.
cues.zh: 这种商品最终会落到谁手里？在米慎区，租金管制让一些长期租客在市价飙升时仍能安居。但租金管制抑制了新房建设，只是推迟了居民被迫搬迁的时间。租客一旦去世或搬走，房东想涨多少租金都可以。就社区而言，这个项目只提供了极少量的平价房。这对我们的拉丁裔社区毫无包容性。

cues.en: Rent control wouldn't apply to Tillman's project, but the city requires that all new buildings set aside a portion of their apartments for subsidized affordable housing. In this case, 11 percent of the units would be available only to families that earn less than 55 percent of the area's median income. Organizers with Calle Bendiguatro said this wasn't nearly enough. They either want to block market right housing or to get it converted into 100 percent affordable housing.
cues.zh: 租金管制并不适用于 Tillman 的项目，但市政府要求所有新建建筑都必须留出一部分作为补贴平价房。在这个项目中，只有 11% 的套房专供收入低于当地中位数 55% 的家庭。Calle Bendiguatro 的组织者表示这远远不够。他们要么想阻止市价住房，要么想将其完全转变为 100% 的平价房。

cues.en: We're asking for a continuance to slow down the project. At Tillman's first hearing before the Planning Commission, advocates asked for another delay to work out a deal for him to sell the laundry to a nonprofit that would use donations and government subsidies to build 100 percent affordable housing. If we as a society are going to say we're going to take trillions of public dollars and build affordable housing, I think that is a lovely utopian idea. I don't think it's realistic.
cues.zh: “我们请求延期以放缓项目进度。”在 Tillman 参加规划委员会的首次听证会上，倡导人士要求再次延期，以便协商让他将洗衣店卖给一家非营利机构，由后者利用捐款和政府补贴建造 100% 的平价房。“如果我们全社会要说拿出数万亿美元的公共资金来建平价房，我觉得这是个美好的乌托邦想法。但我认为这不切实际。”

cues.en: David thinks that anti-gentrification groups are forcing their communities into a false choice. If one is truly an affordable housing advocate, that person should say, we need to figure out a way to speed up the production of market rate housing. Because the fees that we get from market rate housing is the quickest way that we can fund affordable housing.
cues.zh: David认为，反绅士化团体正迫使自己的社区接受一个虚假的选择。如果一个人真是可负担住房倡导者，就该说：我们得想办法加快市场价住房的建设。因为从市场价住房获得的费用，是我们资助可负担住房的最快方式。

cues.en: In November 2017, the Planning Commission approved Tillman's project over fierce objections. Sir, I really prefer not to call the sheriff's office. After the commissioners rejected another delay, Caliente Guatro appealed the ruling to the San Francisco Board of Supervisors, who would have the final say. The process would take another seven months. We should do this thoughtfully because the future of San Francisco and the mission is at stake. Tillman's hearing before the supervisors finally happened in June of 2018.
cues.zh: 2017年11月，规划委员会不顾强烈反对，批准了Tillman的项目。先生，我真的不想叫治安官办公室。委员们再次拒绝延期后，Caliente Guatro将该裁决上诉至旧金山市参事会，由后者拥有最终决定权。这一过程又要再花七个月。我们应当审慎行事，因为旧金山的未来和Mission区都岌岌可危。Tillman在市参事会前的听证会终于在2018年6月举行。

cues.en: Four and a half years after he began the process, activists again arrived en masse and the proceedings quickly turned ugly. These are the times that each of us must rise to counteract the terror of rising fascism. There was an activist at that meeting who literally told my daughter that she wished my daughter had been blown up in the Boston bombing. Another activist at that meeting said to one of my gay supporters publicly, we don't want people like you in the mission. Go back to the Castro.
cues.zh: 在他启动这一流程四年半后，活动人士再次成群到场，会议很快变得难堪。此时此刻，我们每个人都必须站出来，对抗不断抬头之法西斯主义的恐怖。会上有一名活动人士真的对我女儿说，她希望我女儿在波士顿爆炸案中被炸死。会上另一名活动人士公开对我的一位同性恋支持者说，我们不想在Mission区看到你这样的人。回Castro去。

cues.en: In San Francisco, everyone's Democrats, but we really have two political parties. We have the progressive political party and we have a moderate political party. The San Francisco Progressive Party is about as anti-progressive as from a policy point of view. They are the party of death. They are the let's pour amber over the city and stop. It's the crisis on Mission Street, upscale cafes coming in, a climbing gym on Mission Street. What's it going to be like five, ten years from now?
cues.zh: 在旧金山，人人都是民主党人，但其实我们真有两个政治派别。一个是进步派政党，一个是温和派政党。从政策角度看，旧金山的进步派政党几乎再反进步不过了。他们是“死亡之党”。他们就是那种“给城市浇上琥珀，然后一切停住”的党派。这是 Mission Street 上的危机：高档咖啡馆开进来，Mission Street 上还开了攀岩馆。五年、十年后会变成什么样？

cues.en: If this was just an issue of bureaucracy, it would be frustrating to doable. What kills you is the political uncertainty. All the other supervisors will back a supervisor on a project that only affects that supervisor's district, and they all do it reciprocally for each other. Nobody's saying that newcomers and change isn't welcome. Supervisor Hillary Ronan, who did not respond to our interview request, represents the mission.
cues.zh: 如果这只是官僚流程问题，那虽然让人沮丧，但还是能办。真正要命的是政治上的不确定性。其他市议员都会支持某位市议员提出的、只影响其所在选区的项目，而且大家互相投桃报李。没人说新来者和变化不受欢迎。市议员 Hillary Ronan 代表 Mission 区，她没有回应我们的采访请求。

cues.en: In this district, Hillary Ronan is allied with the anti-gentrification groups. Effectively, they can block projects. They're saying build market rate housing, but when you build enough below market rate housing for the people that have lived in this neighborhood. That's just like, it's either a true misunderstanding of how affordable housing gets paid for, or it's pure bullshit, right? I just don't want, I don't want any housing.
cues.zh: 在这个选区，Hillary Ronan 与反绅士化团体结盟。实际上，他们能拦住项目。他们说建市场价住房可以，但你得为一直住在这个社区的人建够低于市场价的住房。这要么是对可负担住房资金来源的彻底误解，要么就是纯扯淡，对吧？我就是不想，不想建任何住房。

cues.en: I have not been singled out. This is the playbook that they use with everybody. Tillman says he's seen numerous other projects stymied, no matter how small the developer. There was a four unit project at 792 Cap Street that literally went through half a dozen planning commission hearings. The project sponsor was a man named Lucas Eastwood, who is a full-blooded Native American and grew up on a reservation. He employs predominantly Hispanic building crew.
cues.zh: 我并没有被单独针对。这是他们对所有人都用的套路。Tillman说他见过许多其他项目被阻挠，无论开发商规模多小。Cap街792号有一个四单元的项目，居然经历了六次规划委员会听证会。项目发起人叫Lucas Eastwood，是纯血统的印第安人，在保留地长大。他的建筑团队以拉美裔为主。

cues.en: And still, he was delayed and harassed. At Tillman's hearing, Ronan and the other supervisors didn't object to any aspect of his existing application. But they found a new issue that in the over four year process hadn't yet been raised. In terms of shadows. They denied the project because it cast a partial shadow on an adjacent schoolyard.
cues.zh: 即便如此，他还是被拖延和刁难。在Tillman的听证会上，Ronan和其他主管对他现有申请的各个方面都没有异议。但他们找到了一个在四年多的流程中从未被提出的新问题。就是阴影问题。他们否决了项目，因为它对邻近的学校操场投下了部分阴影。

cues.en: We need another study done so that way we can confirm that these children will be able to live and play and develop in the sunlight. The building would cast a shadow over this playground in the early morning and as you can see it's already shaded by a number of tore trees. When the choice between expedited development and the health and safety of a child's life, the answer should be a no-brainer.
cues.zh: 我们需要再做一次研究，以确认这些孩子能够在阳光下生活、玩耍和成长。这栋建筑会在清晨在这片操场上投下阴影，而如你所见，它已经被一些树木遮蔽了。在加快开发与孩子的健康和安全之间做选择时，答案应该显而易见。

cues.en: Supervisor Ronan and the board determined that the shadow impact was a potential violation of an environmental law called CEQA. But according to Tillman, such shadows are not covered by CEQA. They made up a CEQA ground that doesn't exist under their own law objectively. Let's be honest about this is about getting top dollar for a piece of property. Mr. Tillman is exploiting the process for his own personal gain. I follow the laws.
cues.zh: Ronan主管和董事会认定，阴影影响可能违反了名为CEQA的环境法。但据Tillman说，这类阴影并不在CEQA的管辖范围内。他们凭空捏造了一个在他们自己的法律下根本不存在的CEQA依据。说实话，这就是为了把一块地产卖出最高价。Tillman先生是在利用这个流程谋取私利。我是依法办事的。

cues.en: For four and a half years, I've spent $1.2 million following the laws. And now at the last minute, they break their own laws. If you're wondering why housing in San Francisco is expensive, that is why. They make it expensive here. It is intentional. Tillman considers himself lucky to have an existing business that offsets the cost of the delays. Many other developers sit on idle properties as their bills stack up.
cues.zh: 四年半来，我花了120万美元遵守法律。可现在到了最后一刻，他们却违反自己定的法律。如果你想知道旧金山的住房为什么这么贵，原因就在这里。他们让这里的房价变得昂贵。这是故意的。蒂尔曼觉得自己还算幸运，因为他已有业务可以抵消延误带来的成本。许多其他开发商则只能守着闲置的地产，眼看着账单越堆越高。

cues.en: So the question is, well, then why do developers kind of put up with this, right? David says that the Board of Supervisors even commonly ignores mandates and state law to streamline the approval process. Local officials get away with this because the only recourse for developers is to sue the city, and that's extremely rare because they fear retaliation. They can be held hostage on other projects, and the city's laws are complex enough that that's very easy to do.
cues.zh: 所以问题来了，开发商为什么还要忍受这些呢？大卫说，监事会甚至常常无视规定和州法律，而这些法律本是为了简化审批流程。地方官员之所以能这样逍遥法外，是因为开发商唯一的救济途径就是起诉市政府，而这极其罕见，因为他们害怕遭到报复。他们可能在其它项目上被拿捏，而该市的法律又足够复杂，很容易做到这一点。

cues.en: Bob is in a really unique situation. He is a one-time developer. He's never building anything else in San Francisco. The only reason that I am able to sue is because I did not have the constraints on me that other developers do. After the Board of Supervisors rejected his plans, Tillman decided to take San Francisco to court for $17 million in damages, or what he says his building would have generated thus far if not for the city's illegal delays.
cues.zh: 鲍勃的情况非常特殊。他是一位一次性开发商。他不会再在旧金山建任何东西。我之所以能起诉，唯一的原因就是我没有其他开发商所面临的那些束缚。监事会否决了他的计划后，蒂尔曼决定把旧金山市告上法庭，索赔1700万美元的损失，或者说，他声称如果没有该市的非法延误，他的建筑至今本应产生的收益。

cues.en: Even the people who are against Bob's project readily admit to me, well, he's not following the unwritten rules. And I say, well, you know, good. It's about time someone doesn't follow the unwritten rules. Anyone who today is a NIMBY, the not in my backyard movement, is clearly on the wrong side of history.
cues.zh: 就连反对Bob项目的人也坦率地跟我说，嗯，他没遵守那些不成文的规矩。我说，那好啊，是时候有人不守这些不成文规矩了。今天任何一个NIMBY，也就是“别在我家后院”运动的人，显然都站在了历史的错误一边。

cues.en: David views Tillman's case as just one battle in the housing policy war that will determine whether San Francisco continues its transformation into a cloistered country club, or if its future will be as diverse and welcoming as its past. I'm not sure that one wants to be remembered in San Francisco as a person standing up saying, I don't want those people living in my neighborhood. Whether they mean it or not, it's a policy of exclusion. The messaging, the language is changing.
cues.zh: David把Tillman的案子看作住房政策战争中的一场战役，这场战争将决定旧金山是继续变成一个封闭的乡村俱乐部，还是像过去一样多元而包容。我不确定有人会想在旧金山被记住为那个站出来说“我不想让那些人住在我社区”的人。不管他们是不是有意的，这就是一种排斥政策。话术和措辞正在改变。

cues.en: And that is really kind of very, very powerful. The politics kind of lags behind. We have to make changes to our bureaucratic process that gets in the way of housing production in San Francisco. In 2018, San Francisco voters elected Mayor London Breed, who made a campaign promise to streamline the approval of new housing. But Tillman used Breed's past record as a testament to how anti-development groups have captured the local political class.
cues.zh: 这真的非常有力量。政治往往滞后于现实。我们必须改革那些阻碍旧金山住房建设的官僚流程。2018年，旧金山选民选出了市长London Breed，她竞选时承诺要简化新住房的审批流程。但Tillman用Breed过去的记录来证明，反开发团体已经俘获了当地的政治阶层。

cues.en: That's because less than a month before she was sworn in as mayor, Reed cast one of her final votes as president of the Board of Supervisors. It was a vote against Tillman's project. They have made the building of housing more costly and more time-consuming and more uncertain and more difficult in about a dozen different ways. It is far worse than it was in 2014 when I started.
cues.zh: 因为就在她宣誓就任市长不到一个月前，Breed以监事会主席身份投了她最后的几票之一。那一票反对的正是Tillman的项目。他们用十几种不同的方式，让住房建设更昂贵、更耗时、更不确定、更困难。情况比我2014年刚入行时糟糕得多。

cues.en: We have to build more housing. We have to build more housing. We have to build more housing. But soon after Tillman sued in August, the Planning Commission delivered a surprise. We asked the shadow consultant to prepare this. It had independently studied the shadow issue and found that it wouldn't have a significant negative impact on the playground next door. The commission quickly re-approved the project, and Calle Bentiquatro declined to appeal. As of now, it looks like Tillman finally has the green light to move forward.
cues.zh: 我们必须建更多住房。我们必须建更多住房。我们必须建更多住房。但 Tillman 在八月起诉后不久，规划委员会带来了一个意外。我们让阴影顾问准备了这份报告。该顾问独立研究了阴影问题，发现它不会对隔壁的操场造成重大负面影响。委员会迅速重新批准了项目，Calle Bentiquatro 放弃上诉。目前看来，Tillman 终于获准继续推进。

cues.en: more than four and a half years after he began. Still, he hasn't yet withdrawn his lawsuit because he says the Board of Supervisors is continuing to devise ways to try to derail his plans. We're in a hole. And the first rule of holes is when you're in a hole, stop digging.
cues.zh: 此时距他开始已过去四年半多。不过，他仍未撤诉，因为他说监事会仍在设法阻挠他的计划。我们掉进坑里了。而坑的第一条规则是：当你掉进坑里，就别再挖了。
